answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake that grows with its workload history, so spawning thousands of fake agents becomes expensive while honest ones earn the stake back. Like a comet that only passes once, the stake is time-bound: it unlocks slowly, so an attacker must tie up capital for weeks to flood the market. A lightweight reputation signal, as hard to fake as tracing a zephyr through a canyon, then ranks agents by verified completed work, letting newcomers prove themselves cheaply on small tasks before touching valuable ones.
